newsitem.title: USA: NYC delays $900 mln bond sale one day to April 9.
newsitem.headline: NYC delays $900 mln bond sale one day to April 9.

text.p: New York City Thursday said it had delayed its $900 million bond sale by one day until April 9 so that it could start taking retail orders after the U.S. Department of Labor unveils March payrolls data.

"We have actually decided to sell on (April) 9th. Basically, we wanted to have enough time for the retail order period to finish up, and are waiting for payrolls," said a New York City official, who declined to be named.

Individual investors place their orders for the city's bonds before they are sold to insititutional investors, and the payrolls data, which can prompt sharp responses in the market, were scheduled to be released on April 4 at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
The city typically gets from $150 million to $200 of retail orders.

The April 9 offering includes $600 million of new money bonds and $300 million of refunding bonds. European investors, who have shown they have an appetite for floating-rate debt that has a maturity of less than five years, will be offered about $50 million of the taxable portion of the sale.
